newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-CARSTENSEN WINS MEN'S 400 FREESTYLE WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-CARSTENSEN WINS MEN'S 400 FREESTYLE WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Denmark's Jacob Carstensen produced a storming finish to snatch the men's 400 metres freestyle title in a desperately close-fought final at the world short-course swimming championships on Friday.
The lead had swapped hands among four other swimmers until the final 50 metres but it was the 18-year-old Dane who burst through when it mattered and claimed the gold.
A mere 0.49 seconds separated the top five at the end of the 16-length race in the 25-metre Scandinavium arena pool.
Carstensen grabbed the gold in three minutes 43.44 seconds, with American Chad Carvin second in 3:43.73 and Australia's Grant Hackett third in 3:43.83.
Britain's Paul Palmer, silver medallist at last year's Olympics when Carstensen touched eighth, led with 50 metres to go but finished outside the medals in fourth place in 3:43.90.

German veteran Joerg Hoffmann, the European record holder and fastest qualifier, duelled with Hackett for control in the first half of the race but was ultimately relegated to fifth, 0.03 seconds behind Palmer.
